newsitem.title: USA: Large-cap stocks outpace small caps in Q3 - Russell.
newsitem.headline: Large-cap stocks outpace small caps in Q3 - Russell.

text.p: Large cap issues proved more resilient than their small-cap counterparts, as U.S. stocks weathered a broad decline in July, according to data compiled by the Frank Russell Co.
The Russell 3000 index, which measures 98 percent of the investable U.S. stock market, rose 2.95 percent in the quarter, bringing the year-to-date return to 13.11 percent.
"As is common during market declines, large stocks held up better than smaller issues," said Paul Greenwood, senior research analyst at Russell.
The Russell 3000 index fell 5.24 percent in July, rose 3.03 percent in August and gained 5.44 percent in September.

The Russell 2000 index of small company stocks returned 0.34 percent in the quarter and 10.73 percent in the year to date. For July, it lost 8.73 percent; in August it gained 5.81 percent; and in September it gained 3.91 percent.
The technology sector within the Russell 3000 index lost 6.88 percent in July, but ended the full quarter with a gain of 8.33 percent.
